podcast.title: Appearance at Memphis Charity Show
podcast.body: BB King was part of the almost entirely black lineup at a charity Christmas show in Memphis for impoverished black youth, where LC Cook and Elvis Presley also appeared. "The lineup of the show was almost entirely black. People like Ray Charles, BB King, Rufus Thomas and so on."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty: "You Send Me" by Sam Cooke

podcast.title: Blues Club Patronage
podcast.body: As a child, Jerry Lee Lewis would regularly sneak into a local blues club with an entirely Black clientele to watch performers like BB King, Fats Domino, Charles Brown, and Big Joe Turner until he was kicked out by the owner in the segregated South. "he would regularly sneak into a local blues club with an otherwise entirely black-cli-on-tail and hide under the table to watch people like Fat Stummino, Charles Brown, BB King, and Big Joe Turner."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 59: "Whole Lotta Shakin' Goin' On" by Jerry Lee Lewis

podcast.title: Influenced by Tharp
podcast.body: BB King was among the musicians who adapted the electric guitar style invented by Sister Rosetta Tharp. "she more or less invented the guitar style that T-bone Walker, BB King and others, would adapt for themselves."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 5: "This Train" by Sister Rosetta Tharpe

podcast.title: Musical Authority
podcast.body: Jerry Lee Lewis, despite being surprisingly ignorant in other matters outside of the Bible and comics, could talk with significant authority about the musical techniques of everyone from BB King to Frank Sinatra. "He could talk with a huge amount of authority about the musical techniques of everyone from BB King to Frank Sinatra."
